name: Orders
description: Sales and purchase orders (doc_type on one shared schema, the real SO/PO split): owner-scoped CRUD, guarded status lifecycle (draft/confirmed/processing/shipped/delivered/cancelled), and a HANDLES totals handler (system_order_totals) that stamps subtotal/tax/total from order_lines in integer cents on every line change. Order lines optionally relate to app-catalog's products collection but do not require it -- a line may be free-text. Reconciled against a private predecessor-system audit, not part of this repo. Deferred to a later slice: auto-numbered sequences per doc_type (an order_counters collection + a closed orders create route), the convert_to_invoice ACTION (invoice_id exists on orders so the provenance link has somewhere to land once that flow is built), stock decrement on ship, and purchase-order receiving. subtotal_cents/tax_cents/total_cents/line_total_cents/line_tax_cents are deliberately NOT schema read_only -- see objects/system/order_totals.py's module docstring for why (update_collection_record has no read_only write exception, so a truly read_only field could never be re-stamped). The order permalink /orders/{order_id:uuid} is now a seeded 59 detail view (site_view_render): a composed page of three generic block renderers -- an editable+deletable `detail` block (the order; money renders via /form's cents formatting, no custom JS, and status transitions become status-field edits in the owner edit form, guarded by the 10-flow transitions above -- no one-click status buttons, the same make-it-basic trade app-forum's pin/lock takes), a `related` block (order_lines flat by order_id), and a `form` block with fixed:{order_id:$record_id} (Add Line, FK locked to the page's order). order_lines stays a RELATIONAL collection, not embedded on orders -- a line is addressable on its own (it can have things attached to it later), matching every other line-item package here (app-invoices' invoice_lines, app-forum's forum_replies). No bespoke per-order page. 0.3.0 deletes the bespoke /orders list page object too: it was ~90 lines of chrome around two generator calls with no business logic of its own, and is now a seeded VIEW record over the same `list` block the order detail's own retrofit already established the precedent for. Ships an attention provider for committed orders with goods still owed -- the pick queue as a number. site_pick_list folds the same arithmetic live and is right to, because it is a working screen somebody opens on purpose; a home page cannot afford that fold a dozen times over, so the daemon runs this on an interval instead. The status set and the shipped-quantity rule are read from site_pick_list so the badge and the page it links to cannot disagree. 0.5.0 gives the CUSTOMER a voice back. Until now a guest paid and heard silence: there was no transactional email anywhere on this server and no way for a buyer without an account to ask where their order was. orders.portal_token (v5 of the schema, read_only like the invoice one) is that missing door -- an unguessable capability URL minted by system_order_portal_link the moment an order stops being a draft, and synchronously by app-shop's action_checkout so the checkout response can hand the shopper the link while they are still standing there. site_order_status renders it at /orders/track/{token}, PUBLIC: order number, date, the itemised receipt with prices (unlike the packing slip, which carries none because it goes in the box), the status translated out of warehouse vocabulary into words a person waiting for a parcel understands, the carrier and tracking number when a shipment has them, the pay link while the bill is open, and a return link carrying the same token once something has shipped. Looked up by token only with a constant-time compare; an unknown token gets a friendly 404 that never hints another one would have worked. system_order_email composes the three messages a shop owes a buyer -- confirmed, shipped, refunded -- each fired by a TRANSITION rather than a button, because a button is a thing somebody forgets on a busy Friday. It QUEUES into app-email's outbox and never sends inline, so a slow relay cannot slow the write that triggered it, and it is idempotent by provenance: the marker lives in the outbox row's source_object_id, so a replayed event composes nothing. No nav entry for the tracking page and none wanted -- it is a per-record customer document, not a door into the app, and this package already declares its front door at /orders. No new dependencies either: the email, shipment and invoice reads are all wrapped, because app-shipping already depends on app-orders and the arrow cannot point both ways.
